articles.title: Rasuwa floods weigh on Nepal’s stock market as hydropower, insurers slide
articles.summary: Heavy rains caused flooding in Rasuwa District, damaging several hydropower projects and affecting non‑life insurance operations. The damage reports triggered a sharp sell‑off in related stocks, pulling the Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) index down by 35.92 points, or 1.38%. Investors reacted negatively as both the hydropower sector and insurers faced heightened risk, highlighting the vulnerability of Nepal’s infrastructure‑dependent market to extreme weather events.

articles.title: What we know about the Bhotekoshi flood so far
articles.summary: The Bhotekoshi flood has resulted in 22 deaths, nearly 400 missing, and 88 rescued, with search-and-rescue efforts hindered by inclement weather and communication disruptions.

articles.title: Bhotekoshi flood sweeps away nine bank branches, 26 staff out of contact
articles.summary: A severe flood in the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa district swept away nine commercial bank branches, leaving 26 staff members out of contact. The Nepal Bankers’ Association reported that communication disruptions are hampering efforts to locate the employees and assess the damage.

articles.title: At least 14 infants killed in Islamabad hospital fire
articles.summary: A fire at a hospital in Islamabad's neonatal ward killed at least 14 infants, with television footage showing a gutted, blackened ward, scattered equipment and lingering smoke.

articles.title: UPDATE: Rasuwa flood death toll climbs to 95 as dozens remain missing
articles.summary: The death toll from the recent floods in Nepal’s Rasuwa district has risen to 95, with dozens still missing. The Prime Minister's Office reports fatalities across seven districts, and many individuals—including security personnel, hydropower workers, customs staff and bank employees—remain out of contact after the Wednesday flooding. Rescue and relief operations continue as authorities assess the full impact of the disaster.

articles.title: Nepal seeks answers on flash flood as India, China, US and World Bank offer support
articles.summary: A flash flood in Nepal, possibly caused by a glacial outburst triggered by an earthquake in Tibet, has prompted urgent rescue and relief operations. While Nepalese and Chinese officials have yet to confirm the exact cause, the disaster has drawn offers of assistance from India, China, the United States and the World Bank. International aid teams are preparing to support affected communities as authorities continue investigations into the event.

articles.title: Ice avalanche, debris lake may have triggered Bhotekoshi flood
articles.summary: Satellite imagery released by Chinese authorities shows that an ice avalanche and a debris lake blocked the Bhotekoshi River about 20 kilometres upstream of the Miteri Bridge. The blockage caused water to accumulate until a sudden breach released a powerful surge that swept downstream, resulting in severe flooding in the Bhotekoshi basin. Local officials are investigating the event, which has damaged infrastructure, displaced residents, and raised concerns about future glacial lake outburst floods in the Himalayan region.

articles.title: Are promises to depoliticise universities truly being fulfilled?
articles.summary: The article scrutinizes the Nepalese government's pledge to depoliticise university governance, arguing that recent vice‑chancellor appointments still appear driven by political favour rather than merit. It highlights specific cases where candidates with strong political connections were selected, cites concerns from academic bodies and scholars about the lack of transparent, merit‑based processes, and references statements from the Ministry of Education and the University Grants Commission. The piece calls for clear, impartial criteria and stronger institutional autonomy to ensure universities serve academic rather than partisan interests.

articles.title: Why Nepal’s infrastructure keeps getting devoured by rivers
articles.summary: The article examines why Nepal’s roads, bridges and other infrastructure are repeatedly destroyed by river floods. It argues that outdated planning assumes a stable, calm river system, ignoring the intensified monsoon rains and glacial melt driven by climate change. Weak design standards, insufficient drainage, and a lack of coordinated investment among ministries leave critical assets vulnerable. The piece calls for a shift toward resilient, flood‑aware engineering, better data sharing, and stronger political will to prioritize adaptation before the next disaster strikes.

articles.title: Strengthen early-warning systems, fix cross-border information sharing
articles.summary: Repeated floods and glacial lake outburst floods have highlighted Nepal's susceptibility to climate‑related disasters. Experts and officials call for stronger early‑warning systems and better cross‑border information sharing with neighboring countries to improve preparedness and reduce loss of life and property. The article stresses the need for coordinated policies, investment in technology, and regular data exchange to mitigate future hazards.

articles.title: Flood death toll continues to rise as Nepal reels from one of its worst disasters in years
articles.summary: A sudden avalanche on the Chinese side of the border unleashed a massive wall of water that surged down the Bhotekoshi River, flooding trekking routes and towns in Nepal. The disaster, one of the worst in recent years, has caused the death toll to continue rising as rescue efforts struggle against the swift currents and landslides. Communities along the river are grappling with loss of life, property damage, and displacement, while authorities coordinate emergency response and seek aid to address the growing humanitarian crisis.

articles.title: Rare honeyguide adds to Ilam’s growing birdwatching appeal
articles.summary: A recent birdwatching expedition in Ilam, eastern Nepal, recorded 74 bird species, including the rare and endangered yellow‑rumped honeyguide. The sighting highlights Ilam’s growing reputation as a prime destination for birdwatchers and underscores the region’s biodiversity. Local tourism officials and conservation groups are promoting the find to attract eco‑tourists and raise awareness about protecting threatened habitats. The discovery is expected to boost community‑based tourism and support ongoing conservation efforts in the area.

articles.title: Fast delivery changes the game for Nepal’s online sellers
articles.summary: New delivery platforms in Nepal are reshaping e‑commerce by offering ultra‑fast shipping options that appeal to time‑conscious shoppers and enable small merchants to reach customers more efficiently. By simplifying order fulfillment and reducing logistics costs, these services are encouraging more local businesses to go online and compete with larger retailers. The trend is boosting consumer confidence in digital shopping and prompting traditional sellers to adopt faster, tech‑driven solutions.

articles.title: Thousands chase 14 spots for Nepal’s FIFA U15 World Cup squad
articles.summary: A massive response from young footballers has emerged as Nepal prepares to select its 14-player squad for the FIFA U15 World Cup, highlighting the enthusiasm at the grassroots level. However, the article points out a stark contrast with the lack of adequate support and resources from the government, raising concerns about neglect of youth development in the sport. The selection process underscores both the hope for international representation and the challenges faced by Nepali football due to insufficient institutional backing.

articles.title: Meta agrees to pay $18 billion to settle US lawsuits over children’s social media addiction
articles.summary: Meta Platforms agreed to pay $18 billion to resolve multiple U.S. lawsuits alleging that its platforms fostered children’s social‑media addiction. As part of the settlement, Meta will impose new usage limits for teenagers on Facebook and Instagram, capping daily access at two hours and blocking access between midnight and 6 a.m. unless parents give consent. The deal, spanning a decade, aims to curb excessive screen time among minors and addresses growing regulatory and public pressure on tech companies to protect youth.

articles.title: How people can help Nepal’s flood-affected communities
articles.summary: Recent floods have caused widespread damage across Nepal, and aid organizations are urging the public to contribute cash donations rather than physical goods. Cash is considered more efficient for meeting immediate needs such as food, shelter, and medical supplies, allowing NGOs to allocate resources where they are most needed. The scale of destruction is still being evaluated, but the call for monetary support aims to accelerate relief efforts for the affected communities.

articles.title: Balendra Shah heads to flood-hit Nuwakot to assess damage
articles.summary: Prime Minister Balendra Shah traveled to flood‑hit Nuwakot, specifically the town of Bidur, to assess damage caused by recent floods. He inspected the affected areas, met with local officials, and oversaw ongoing rescue, relief, and infrastructure restoration efforts.

articles.title: How the Bhotekoshi flood unfolded over 10 hours
articles.summary: According to the Flood Forecasting Division’s technical report, authorities received information at 9:05 am that a major flood had entered Nepal’s Bhotekoshi River from the Tibetan side, outlining how the flood unfolded over a ten‑hour period.

articles.title: 826 out of contact after Bhotekoshi flood, including 590 tourists
articles.summary: The Bhotekoshi flood in Nepal has left 826 people unaccounted for, including 590 tourists, security personnel, and local residents. The number of missing has risen sharply since the disaster on Wednesday, prompting concern among authorities and families as rescue efforts continue.

articles.title: Nepal, Bangladesh discuss support for flood rescue and relief
articles.summary: Nepal's Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal met with his Bangladeshi counterpart to discuss cooperation on flood rescue and relief efforts. Khanal affirmed that Kathmandu will stay in close contact with Dhaka to coordinate any assistance Nepal may require as it copes with severe flooding. The dialogue underscores bilateral goodwill and the readiness of Bangladesh to support Nepal's disaster response.

articles.title: Kathmandu hospital crowded with families searching for flood-hit relatives
articles.summary: Following devastating floods in Nepal, TU Teaching Hospital in Kathmandu has become a hub for families searching for missing relatives. The hospital has set up information desks and posted lists of survivors and the deceased as the search continues for at least 826 people who remain unaccounted for. Crowds of relatives and volunteers fill the corridors, reflecting the widespread impact of the disaster and the urgent need for coordinated rescue and relief efforts.

articles.title: Nepal flood death toll reaches 289 as hundreds remain out of contact
articles.summary: Heavy monsoon floods in Nepal have killed at least 289 people, with hundreds more missing or out of contact. The worst-affected districts are Chitwan, Nawalparasi East and Dhading, where rising waters have destroyed homes and infrastructure. Rescue teams continue search and relief operations, while authorities urge residents to stay vigilant as the disaster response intensifies across the country.

articles.title: Parties call for joint Nepal-China study of glacial lake risks
articles.summary: Eight political parties in Nepal have called for a joint Nepal‑China study on the risks posed by glacial lakes. At an all‑party meeting they also agreed to set up a parliamentary mechanism to oversee flood recovery efforts and to advocate for stronger cross‑border early warning systems.

articles.title: Climate change boosted risk of devastating Himalayan flood, experts say
articles.summary: Experts warn that rising temperatures are accelerating glacier melt and destabilising mountain slopes in the Himalayas, heightening the risk of catastrophic floods in Nepal. The combination of climate‑driven warming and fragile terrain creates conditions for cascading disasters, where a glacial lake outburst could trigger downstream landslides and widespread flooding. Authorities are urged to improve early‑warning systems and invest in climate‑resilient infrastructure to mitigate the looming threat.
